name: soft tissue mass overview
title: A soft tissue mass: under 5 cm with no suspicious feature is excised; over 5 cm or with any suspicious feature is imaged and core-biopsied first, then a benign result is observed, a resectable sarcoma is staged and treated by surgery with radiation, and a non-curable one goes to palliative care

nodes.title: A soft tissue lump: could it be a SARCOMA? Decide BEFORE anyone cuts it out
lines: benign tumours are 100 times more common (300 vs 2 per 100 000) · a sarcoma shelled out like a benign lump, with little or no margin, is the 'WHOOPS': less chance of cure, possible amputation

history: has it GROWN? first noticed when, how big then and now (be persistent: fruit, nuts) · trauma · pain or numbness (sarcoma usually painless; big symptoms → metastases) · recurrence · other lumps · family history
exam: location, size, skin · superficial (subcutaneous) or DEEP (muscle) · mobile, tethered or FIXED · nodes rarely involved

nodes.title: Under 5 cm, NO suspicious feature
lines: limited growth · minimal symptoms · superficial

nodes.title: Over 5 cm, OR under 5 cm with ANY suspicious feature
lines: rapid growth · pain · recurrent · deep · fixed · difficult location

nodes.title: IMAGE before biopsy
lines: MRI preferred · CT · rarely ultrasound · or a surgical expert
then CORE biopsy by someone experienced in sarcoma · NOT fine needle aspiration

nodes.title: Low risk
lines: limited growth, minimal symptoms, superficial

nodes.title: Benign on biopsy
lines: e.g. spindle cell/pleomorphic lipoma
case: 33 M, 17 cm flank mass for 6 years, mobile, subcutaneous, many lipomas, uncle too · ultrasound: probable lipoma → MRI

nodes.title: Sarcoma, resectable
lines: usually a PAINLESS lump
curable by surgery + radiation: leiomyosarcoma, liposarcoma

nodes.title: Not curable
lines: e.g. lung metastases, non-resectable

nodes.title: Excisional biopsy is acceptable
lines: complete removal with minimal surrounding tissue
NOT ideal if it is a sarcoma

nodes.title: Lipoma or liposarcoma?
lines: vs well-differentiated liposarcoma (atypical lipomatous tumour)
immunohistochemistry: MDM2 negative, CD34 positive → lipoma

nodes.title: 1 · Stage: CT chest
lines: the lung is where it spreads

nodes.title: 2 · Multidisciplinary tumour board
lines: every possible sarcoma

nodes.title: Medical oncology
lines: no standard chemotherapy · goals of care · clinical trials

nodes.title: Surgery: WIDE resection
lines: a marginal resection is the 'whoops'
wide = 1-2 cm (rare) · close or positive margin common → radiation

nodes.title: ± Radiation, mostly PRE-operative
lines: • local recurrence 30% → 10%
• pre-op: better long-term function: only the tumour radiated, surgery removes the radiated tissue
• case: radiation 6 weeks → surgery 6-8 weeks later

nodes.title: ± Chemotherapy: uncommon
lines: • NOT standard after surgery (no survival gain) · select subtypes, trials
• curable with it: osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma in young adults

nodes.title: Palliative care
lines: can greatly improve quality of life

nodes.title: Follow-up after cure
lines: clinic every 6 months · chest x-ray yearly or CT chest every 6 months
case: 55 M, neurofibromatosis, thigh mass doubled, aching → malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour → lung metastases at 1 year

panels.title: Biopsy options
items: fine needle aspiration: cheap, fast, atraumatic BUT poor yield, hard to type · not for primary diagnosis
excisional: whole lump, little margin · NOT if sarcoma · incisional: more tissue, more invasive
CORE: the best compromise · less invasive, adequate tissue · then expert pathology: histology, immunohistochemistry, cytogenetics, molecular

panels.title: Classification
items: named for the adult tissue it resembles: lipoma/liposarcoma · rhabdomyoma/rhabdomyosarcoma · leiomyoma/leiomyosarcoma · fibroma/fibrosarcoma · neurofibroma/neurofibrosarcoma
benign: may recur, no metastasis · intermediate: locally aggressive, or metastasizes 5-10% · malignant: frequent metastasis
well-differentiated liposarcoma recurs locally only · DEDIFFERENTIATED also metastasizes (case: 55 M abdominal mass, early satiety, 20 lb loss · 5-year survival 40%)
incidence rises with age · children: neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma

panels.title: Causes (99% unknown)
items: asbestos → mesothelioma · vinyl chloride → angiosarcoma · herbicides, dioxin, radiation → undifferentiated
human herpesvirus 8 → Kaposi · chronic lymphedema (Stewart-Treves) → angiosarcoma · trauma → myositis ossificans
